pharm: Irreversibly binds and inhibits the chymotrypsin-like activity of the 20S proteasome, causing accumulation of polyubiquitinated proteins and apoptosis of malignant plasma cells
quick: IV 20 mg/m2 on cycle 1 days 1-2, then escalate to target 27-56 mg/m2 depending on regimen, over 10-30 minutes
Not affected by food; given as an intravenous infusion regardless of meals
Can cause fetal harm; avoid in pregnancy and use effective contraception
Breastfeeding not recommended during and for a period after treatment
Pharmacokinetics not affected by renal function including dialysis; monitor renal function
Reduce starting dose by about 25% in mild-to-moderate impairment; monitor LFTs
No specific interaction; limit alcohol given general illness and hepatic monitoring
Cardiac/blood pressure, renal function, electrolytes, CBC, LFTs, signs of infusion reaction
summary: Carfilzomib is an irreversible proteasome inhibitor used to treat relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma, given intravenously in combination (e.g. with lenalidomide and dexamethasone, daratumumab and dexamethasone, or as monotherapy) or with dexamethasone alone. Cycle 1 begins at 20 mg/m2 on days 1 and 2 and, if tolerated, escalates to a target dose (commonly 27, 56 or 70 mg/m2 depending on the regimen). Key risks include cardiac toxicity (new or worsening heart failure, ischaemia, hypertension including hypertensive crisis), acute infusion reactions, pulmonary toxicity, pulmonary hypertension, renal toxicity/acute kidney injury, tumour lysis syndrome, thrombocytopenia, venous thromboembolism, hepatic toxicity and thrombotic microangiopathy. Dexamethasone premedication and adequate hydration are required, and patients need close cardiac, renal, blood-pressure and haematologic monitoring.
indications: Relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma in combination with dexamethasone, or with lenalidomide and dexamethasone, or with daratumumab/isatuximab and dexamethasone, in patients who have received one to three prior lines of therapy
Relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma as monotherapy in patients who have received one or more prior lines of therapy

dosage.d: 20 mg/m2 IV on days 1 and 2 of cycle 1
dosage.t: IV over 10-30 minutes depending on regimen
dosage.n: Premedicate with dexamethasone; hydrate before and after dosing in early cycles

dosage.d: Escalate to 27 or 56 mg/m2 on days 1, 2, 8, 9, 15 and 16 of each 28-day cycle (regimen-dependent)
dosage.n: 56 mg/m2 dose infused over 30 minutes; dose is based on actual body surface area

dosage.d: After 20 mg/m2 on cycle 1 day 1, escalate to 70 mg/m2 on days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle
dosage.n: Used in the once-weekly Kd and selected combination regimens

dosage.r: Cardiac, renal, hepatic or haematologic toxicity
dosage.d: Withhold and reduce dose stepwise per label for toxicity; resume at a reduced level if recovered
dosage.n: Permanently discontinue for severe or recurrent serious toxicity

admin: Premedicate with dexamethasone (oral or IV) before all cycle 1 doses and the first cycle of escalation to reduce infusion reactions
Hydrate patients (oral and/or IV fluids) before and after dosing, especially in cycle 1, to reduce renal toxicity and tumour lysis risk
Reconstitute and dilute as directed; infuse over 10-30 minutes (or 30 minutes for 56 and 70 mg/m2 doses) - do not give as a bolus
Calculate dose from actual body surface area; cap BSA calculations as specified for very large patients
Monitor blood pressure and cardiac status during and after infusion; have resuscitation support available
Flush the line before and after administration; do not mix with other medicines
moa: Carfilzomib is a tetrapeptide epoxyketone that selectively and irreversibly binds the N-terminal threonine-containing active site of the chymotrypsin-like subunit of the constitutive 20S proteasome and the immunoproteasome. Proteasome inhibition prevents the regulated degradation of ubiquitinated proteins, leading to accumulation of misfolded and regulatory proteins, endoplasmic reticulum stress, cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis. Malignant plasma cells in multiple myeloma are particularly sensitive because of their high rate of protein synthesis and immunoglobulin production.

absolute: Known severe hypersensitivity to carfilzomib or formulation components
relative: Pre-existing cardiac failure, recent myocardial infarction or uncontrolled arrhythmia
Significant pulmonary disease or pulmonary hypertension
Renal impairment with ongoing risk of acute kidney injury
monitor: Cardiac function and fluid status; blood pressure
Serum electrolytes, uric acid and signs of tumour lysis

preg: Carfilzomib can cause fetal harm based on its mechanism and animal data, including embryo-fetal toxicity. It should not be used in pregnancy unless the potential benefit justifies the risk. Women of reproductive potential should use effective contraception during treatment and for a period afterwards, and men with female partners should also use contraception.
lact: It is not known whether carfilzomib is present in human milk. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in a breastfed infant, breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment and for a period after the final dose.
renal: Carfilzomib clearance is not meaningfully affected by renal impairment, including in patients on dialysis, so no specific pharmacokinetic dose adjustment is required; however, acute kidney injury can occur, so renal function should be monitored and the drug withheld for significant renal toxicity. On dialysis days, administer after the dialysis session.
hepatic: Exposure is higher in hepatic impairment; reduce the starting dose by approximately 25% in patients with mild to moderate impairment. Carfilzomib has not been studied in severe hepatic impairment. Monitor liver enzymes and bilirubin, and withhold for significant hepatotoxicity, which can include hepatic failure.

major: Other agents causing cardiotoxicity or QT effects - additive cardiac risk; monitor closely
Live vaccines - avoid in immunosuppressed patients receiving carfilzomib
Hormonal contraceptives may be less reliable due to nausea/vomiting - use additional/non-hormonal methods
moderate: Concomitant immunomodulatory/myelosuppressive agents (lenalidomide, dexamethasone) - additive cytopenias and thrombosis risk; thromboprophylaxis often needed
minor: Carfilzomib is metabolised largely by peptidase and epoxide hydrolysis, so classic CYP-based interactions are limited
interactions.food: No clinically significant food interaction; administered intravenously
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction documented; moderate use given hepatic monitoring
interactions.diagnostics: May cause thrombocytopenia, anaemia, electrolyte and uric acid changes, and elevated liver enzymes/creatinine on laboratory tests

common: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and decreased appetite
Cough, upper respiratory infection and insomnia
serious: Cardiac toxicity - new or worsening heart failure, myocardial ischaemia/infarction, cardiac arrest
Acute infusion reactions (fever, chills, dyspnoea, hypotension, chest tightness)
Pulmonary toxicity (ARDS, pneumonitis) and pulmonary hypertension
Acute renal failure and tumour lysis syndrome
Venous thromboembolism and hepatic toxicity/hepatic failure
Thrombotic microangiopathy/thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura and posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES)
rare: Severe haemorrhage including gastrointestinal and intracranial bleeding
emergency: Acute heart failure, myocardial infarction or cardiac arrest
Tumour lysis syndrome or acute kidney injury

monitoring: Cardiac assessment (symptoms, fluid status, and cardiac evaluation as indicated) before and during treatment
Blood pressure regularly and optimise hypertension control
Renal function (serum creatinine, urine output) before each cycle
Complete blood count frequently for cytopenias
Serum electrolytes, uric acid and signs of tumour lysis, especially in cycle 1
counsel: This medicine is given as a drip to treat your myeloma; you will also take a steroid (dexamethasone) and need to drink/receive extra fluids
Tell staff immediately of chest pain, breathlessness, swelling of legs, rapid weight gain or palpitations - these may signal heart or lung problems
Report fever, chills, rash or dizziness during or after the infusion (infusion reaction)
Report reduced urine output, severe tiredness, easy bruising/bleeding, or yellowing of the skin/eyes
Use effective contraception and do not breastfeed during treatment
Keep all appointments for blood tests and heart/kidney monitoring
pk: Rapid proteasome inhibition within hours of infusion
Plasma concentrations peak at the end of the short IV infusion
Very short - terminal half-life about 1 hour or less, but proteasome inhibition is sustained because binding is irreversible
Pharmacodynamic effect outlasts plasma levels; proteasome activity recovers as new enzyme is synthesised over days
Store vials refrigerated (2-8 C), protect from light; reconstituted/diluted solution per label stability
pearls: Cardiac toxicity is a defining risk - new or worsening heart failure, ischaemia and hypertensive crisis can occur; assess cardiac status and control blood pressure before and during therapy
Acute infusion reactions can occur up to 24 hours after dosing - dexamethasone premedication is mandatory
Hydrate well in cycle 1 to reduce acute kidney injury and tumour lysis syndrome
Despite a very short plasma half-life, proteasome inhibition is prolonged because binding is irreversible
Watch for venous thromboembolism (thromboprophylaxis with combination regimens) and rare thrombotic microangiopathy/PRES
missed: Carfilzomib is given by a healthcare professional on a fixed schedule. If a scheduled dose is missed or delayed, the treating team will reschedule it; do not attempt to make up doses yourself. Tell your clinic if you cannot attend an appointment.
overdose: There is no specific antidote for carfilzomib overdose. Acute toxicity may include hypotension, chills, cardiac and renal effects. Management is supportive with close monitoring of cardiac, renal, blood-pressure and haematologic parameters and treatment of symptoms as they arise.
